title: AutoRole-Tiny
subtitle: Autonomous role allocation for homogeneous TinyML swarms
summary: A distributed TinyML and embedded CPS framework in which homogeneous MCU sensor nodes autonomously assume complementary roles.
motivation: MCU swarms are often deployed with identical hardware but face changing sensing, communication, and energy conditions. Fixed roles limit their ability to adapt.
problem: How can homogeneous, resource-constrained nodes allocate roles locally while preserving system-level coordination and reliability?
method: Explore decentralized state exchange, local utility estimation, lightweight role negotiation, and embedded evaluation under realistic communication constraints.
results: Ongoing: system architecture, node communication, and role-allocation experiments.

title: FireGuard
subtitle: Edge-assisted multimodal early warning for underground EV fires
summary: An edge-assisted fire early-warning system that combines thermal, gas, and flame sensing for underground electric-vehicle safety.
motivation: Early-stage EV fire signals are heterogeneous and can be difficult to distinguish using a single sensor modality.
problem: How can multiple low-cost sensing modalities be fused near the source to improve timeliness and robustness without depending entirely on the cloud?
method: Combine thermal imagery and environmental sensing through an edge–device architecture for multimodal event detection and warning.
results: System-level research prototype for underground EV fire-safety scenarios.

title: Driver Fatigue Multimodal Detection
subtitle: Multimodal driver behaviour understanding for transportation safety
summary: A multimodal driver-monitoring system combining visual, audio, and environmental cues to understand fatigue-related behaviour.
motivation: Fatigue manifests differently across drivers and operating conditions, making single-modality detection brittle.
problem: How can heterogeneous in-cabin signals be combined to improve robustness while remaining suitable for practical deployment?
method: Integrate computer vision, audio sensing, and environmental measurements into a multimodal perception pipeline.
results: Research system and first-inventor patent contribution.
